newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama jobless rate little changed in '96 - official.
newsitem.headline: Panama jobless rate little changed in '96 - official.

text.p: Panama's unemployment rate stood at 13.9 percent at the end of 1996, compared with 14 percent a year earlier, Planning and Economic Policy Minister Guillermo Chapman told Reuters in an interview Tuesday.
About two-fifths of the nation's 2.5 million inhabitants live in extreme poverty, or about 39 percent, down from 45 percent in 1990, Chapman said.
"These numbers are still extraordinarily high, and no one would say they're acceptable, but this is something the government is attacking and it cannot be solved overnight," he said.
Panama's per capita income averages $3,200 per year, higher than any of its Central American neighbors, Chapman said.
But Panama also has one of the most uneven income distributions in the continent, according to the United Nations. Most Panamanians earn less than $200 a month.

President Ernesto Perez Balladares, who took office in 1994, has pledged to help Panama's poor and open the country's closed economy to trade by reducing tariffs, privatizing state enterprises and strengthening banking laws.

Higher exports could also offset the economic impact of a pull-out of U.S. troops by the year 2000. Panama is expected to lose up to $370 million a year in income, about 5 to 13 percent of its GDP, experts said.
